modules.scope:
The whole product at pin 3eaa79cf: the Python package iris_vector_graph, the IRIS classes under
iris_src/src, the HTTP and GraphQL API under api, and the SQL under sql. This file holds the terms every module
uses and the universal rules (playbook §3.3a step 1) that every module's statements trace to.

Setup of a namespace and its upgrades. The schema name and its record (iris_vector_graph/schema_name.py), setup
itself (initialize_schema and its helpers in iris_vector_graph/_engine/schema.py; the DDL, the deploy entry, the 3.2.0
edge rescue and the graph_id upgrade steps in iris_vector_graph/schema.py), the class deploy
(iris_vector_graph/_engine/class_deploy.py), the routine record (iris_vector_graph/routine_record.py), the legacy
objects (iris_vector_graph/legacy_manifest.py, legacy_bodies.py, legacy_text.py, iris_vector_graph/_engine/legacy.py),
the migration package except the four step modules other modules own (iris_vector_graph/migrations/__init__.py,
_commit.py, statements.py, upgrade.py), the SQL files under sql/, and the server classes Graph.KG.SqlPrivilege and
Graph.KG.SqlProcs. The vector width rules of setup are stated in module VEC; the adjacency hooks in ADJ; the dropping of
compiled query classes in NAT. Evidence is reading at pin 3eaa79cf. Unit tests named here run on fakes and inspect
Python or source text; e2e and integration tests need a live IRIS and were opened, not run.

Production files: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/GraphKey.cls, iris_src/src/Graph/KG/GraphMode.cls, iris_vector_graph/_validate.py (graph-name and input validation), the graph-scoping parts of iris_vector_graph/engine.py, and the mode commands set_multigraph / is_multigraph in iris_vector_graph/_engine/admin.py. The ledger, Bolt, verify and Cypher surfaces are cited only where they decide graph scope or edge identity; their own behaviour belongs to their modules.

Direct (non-ledger) writes of nodes, edges, labels and properties, their write transactions, and bulk loads. Production files: iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py (all but erase_graph, delete_nodes_by_prefix and drop_graph, which the erasure module owns), iris_src/src/Graph/KG/PropWrite.cls, iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Txn.cls, iris_src/src/Graph/KG/LabelIndex.cls, iris_vector_graph/_write_txn.py, iris_vector_graph/bulk_loader.py, iris_vector_graph/prop_values.py, iris_vector_graph/_dictionary.py, iris_vector_graph/_collation.py, iris_vector_graph/_batch_check.py, and the write facade of iris_vector_graph/engine.py. The native adjacency of every graph and what is derived from it. Production files:
iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adjacency.cls (the one writer), AdjIndex.cls (the row hook on rdf_edges), Adj.cls (degree reads
and the degree cache), EdgeScan.cls (scans and the old write names, now delegations), Edgeless.cls (nodes with no
edge), GraphIndex.cls (interning helpers of the interned snapshot), TraversalBuild.cls (BuildKG, BuildNKG, two-hop
counts), GraphVerify.cls (verify_graph), AlgoCache.cls (the result cache); iris_vector_graph/_edgeless.py,
freshness.py, algo_cache.py; and the engine's sync, rebuild, verify and status entry points

not_implemented.text: The graph check reports any graph that already holds the name 0.
In a multigraph, a direct edge create adds a new edge each time.
A direct edge create can hand back the id of the new edge.
The ledger tells parallel edges apart. A change that names a triple with several edges is refused.
A Bolt client sees one id per parallel edge, the same in every process.
When the word index is missing and an index named default exists, the docs table search uses BM25.
When a graph holds two edges with the same tuple, each has its own statement id. A change can name either one.
An execution context would let a session touch one graph only. It is planned and not built.
